metadata.title: On a new proof of the key step in the proof of Brouwer's fixed point theorem

nodes.name: Partial derivative notation $D_i u$
nodes.statement: For real-valued $u(x)$ on $\bR^{d}$, $D_{i}u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial x^{i}}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Notation for the partial derivative of a real-valued function with respect to the $i$-th coordinate.

nodes.name: Jacobian matrix $DF$
nodes.statement: If $F=(F^{i})$ is a smooth mapping of $\bR^{d}$ to $\bR^{d}$, set $DF=(a^{ij})_{i,j=1}^{d}$ with $a^{ij}=D_{j}F^{i}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The Jacobian of a smooth $\bR^{d}$-valued mapping is the matrix of its partial derivatives.

nodes.name: Perturbed mapping $F_{t}$
nodes.statement: For a $C^{1}$ mapping $F:\bar\Omega\to\bR^{d}$ and small $t$, set $F_{t}(x)=tF(x)+x$.
nodes.statement_clean: A one-parameter family of perturbations of the identity by $F$.

nodes.name: Equality of Jacobian integrals for boundary-matching maps (Lemma 3.21.1)
nodes.statement: Let $\Omega$ be a connected bounded domain in $\bR^{d}$ with $C^{1}$ boundary and let $F,G:\bar\Omega\to\bR^{d}$ be $C^{1}(\bar\Omega)$ mappings such that $F=G$ on $\partial\Omega$. Then $\int_{\Omega}\det DF\,dx=\int_{\Omega}\det DG\,dx$.
nodes.statement_clean: Two $C^{1}$ self-maps of a smooth bounded domain that agree on the boundary have equal integrals of their Jacobian determinants.
assumptions: $\Omega$ is a connected bounded domain in $\bR^{d}$ with $C^{1}$ boundary

nodes.name: Polynomial-in-$t$ identity for $\det(tDF+I)$
nodes.statement: $\int_{\Omega}\det(tDF+I)\,dx=\int_{\Omega}\det(tDG+I)\,dx$ for small $t$ (equation (3.21.1)).
nodes.statement_clean: Equality of two polynomials in $t$ obtained from $\mathrm{Vol}\,F_{t}(\Omega)=\mathrm{Vol}\,G_{t}(\Omega)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.21.1
nodes.statement: Show $F_{t}=tF+x$ and $G_{t}=tG+x$ are one-to-one with the same image for small $t$, deduce $\mathrm{Vol}\,F_{t}(\Omega)=\mathrm{Vol}\,G_{t}(\Omega)$, then equate coefficients of the polynomial $\det(tDF+I)$ in $t^{d}$.

nodes.name: Injectivity of $F_{t}$ for small $t$
nodes.statement: By the implicit function theorem, for small $t$ the maps $F_{t}=tF+x$ and $G_{t}=tG+x$ are one-to-one on $\bar\Omega$ and have $C^{1}$ inverses on $\Omega$.

nodes.name: Boundary maps to boundary
nodes.statement: Hence $F_{t}$ and $G_{t}$ map $\partial\Omega$ onto $\partial F_{t}(\Omega)=\partial G_{t}(\Omega)$.

nodes.name: Images coincide and have equal volume
nodes.statement: Since $F_{t}(\Omega)\cap G_{t}(\Omega)\ne\emptyset$ and both connected sets share the same boundary, $F_{t}(\Omega)=G_{t}(\Omega)$ and so $\mathrm{Vol}\,F_{t}(\Omega)=\mathrm{Vol}\,G_{t}(\Omega)$.

nodes.name: Polynomial identification in $t$
nodes.statement: Express the volume identity as $\int_{\Omega}\det(tDF+I)\,dx=\int_{\Omega}\det(tDG+I)\,dx$; both sides are polynomials in $t$, so they agree identically. Comparing coefficients of $t^{d}$ yields $\int_{\Omega}\det DF\,dx=\int_{\Omega}\det DG\,dx$.

nodes.name: Justification of gaps in the proof of Lemma 3.21.1 (Remark 3.21.2)
nodes.statement: Justifies (i) injectivity of $F_{t}$ via Lipschitz estimate $|x'-x''|\leq tN_{F}|x'-x''|$ for $tN_{F}\leq 1/2$; (ii) $F_{t}(\partial\Omega)=\partial F_{t}(\Omega)$ by the open mapping property and a contradiction argument; (iii) $F_{t}(\Omega)=G_{t}(\Omega)$ via Banach-style fixed-point iteration $x_{k+1}=x_{0}+tF(x_{0})-tG(x_{k})$ together with a connectedness/broken-line argument.

nodes.name: Analytic alternative via cofactor identity and Stokes
nodes.statement: For smoother $H$ one has $\det DH=(1/d)\,\mathrm{div}\,\hat H$ with $\hat H_{j}=H^{i}A_{ij}$ and $\sum_{j}D_{j}A_{ij}=0$, so $\frac{d}{dt}\det D[tF+(1-t)G]$ is a divergence whose boundary integral vanishes since $A_{ij}[F^{i}-G^{i}]=0$ on $\partial\Omega$; this is the Stokes-theorem-based proof of Lemma 3.21.1.

nodes.name: No $C^{1}$ retraction onto the boundary (Corollary 3.21.1)
nodes.statement: For the domain $\Omega$ of Lemma 3.21.1 there is no $C^{1}(\bar\Omega)$ map $G:\bar\Omega\to\partial\Omega$ with $G(x)=x$ on $\partial\Omega$.
nodes.statement_clean: No smooth retraction of a smooth bounded domain onto its boundary exists.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.21.1
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 3.21.1 with $F(x)=x$ to get $\mathrm{Vol}\,\Omega=\int_{\Omega}\det DG\,dx$; but the columns of $DG$ are tangent to $\partial\Omega$, hence linearly dependent, so $\det DG=0$, contradicting $\mathrm{Vol}\,\Omega>0$.

nodes.name: Brouwer's fixed point theorem (Theorem 3.21.1)
nodes.statement: Let $B$ be the closed unit ball centered at the origin and let $f:\bar B\to\bar B$ be a continuous mapping. Then $f$ has fixed points in $\bar B$.
nodes.statement_clean: Every continuous self-map of the closed unit ball in $\bR^{d}$ has a fixed point.
assumptions: $B \subset \bR^{d}$ is the closed unit ball centered at the origin
conclusions: $f$ has a fixed point in $\bar B$

nodes.name: Proof of Brouwer's fixed point theorem
nodes.statement: First treat smooth $f$: assuming no fixed point, construct a $C^{1}$ retraction $G(x)=x-t(x)(f(x)-x)$ from $\bar B$ to $\partial B$, contradicting Corollary 3.21.1. Then approximate continuous $f$ by polynomials $f_{n}$ and take a convergent subsequence of fixed points.

nodes.name: Construct candidate retraction $G$
nodes.statement: Assume $f$ smooth and fixed-point-free. For $x\in\bar B$, define $G(x)=x-t(x)(f(x)-x)$ where $t(x)\geq 0$ solves $|x-t(f(x)-x)|=1$.

nodes.name: Smoothness of $t(x)$ via quadratic formula
nodes.statement: The discriminant of the quadratic $|x|^{2}-2t(x,f(x)-x)+t^{2}|f(x)-x|^{2}=1$ is strictly positive and smooth, giving the closed form $t(x)=\frac{(x,f(x)-x)+\sqrt{(x,f(x)-x)^{2}+(1-|x|^{2})|f(x)-x|^{2}}}{|f(x)-x|^{2}}$, hence $G$ is $C^{1}$.

nodes.name: Apply Corollary 3.21.1 (smooth case)
nodes.statement: $G$ is a $C^{1}(\bar B)$ map onto $\partial B$ with $G|_{\partial B}=\mathrm{id}$, contradicting Corollary 3.21.1. So smooth $f$ has a fixed point.

nodes.name: Polynomial approximation (general continuous case)
nodes.statement: Choose polynomials $f_{n}$ with $|f_{n}-f|\leq 1/n$ on $\bar B$, rescale by $n/(n+1)$ so $f_{n}:\bar B\to\bar B$, get fixed points $x_{n}$ from the smooth case, and pass to a convergent subsequence to obtain a fixed point of $f$.
